column4: The section cites 13:2 for the raised heavens; this next ayah turns to the earth spread out, mountains made firm, and rivers, extending the same ordered sky-and-earth scene. Its contribution is the ground below the raised sky.
After the section’s cited 55:7 places the balance, this ayah says not to transgress in it; it supplies the first boundary for the balance image that the section names.
The section cites 55:7’s placed balance; this next ayah commands just weighing and forbids making the balance deficient, specifying what that placed measure does.

The section connects the undoing of a firm tie to breaking oaths; this continuation warns against using oaths deceptively and describes a foot slipping after it was firmly set. 16:91–92 state the oath and yarn images; this ayah adds the consequence of instability.

The section cites 50:7 for earth spread and mountains cast into it; this preceding ayah asks readers to look at the sky above and how it was built and adorned, completing the same constructed-sky/ground scene.
After the section’s cited 51:47 says the sky was built, this next ayah says the earth was spread out, joining the sky’s construction to the ground in one passage.

The section describes a load making the back sound as if a structure were cracking and gives building erection as a dictionary sense; here a wall is on the verge of collapse and Khidr restores it (“فَأَقَامَهُ”), a specific reversal from failing structure to upright structure.

The section’s command to stand is followed by turning toward the Lord and by raised remembrance; this verse commands the Prophet’s night vigil and connects it to the Lord’s promise of a praised station, joining devotional stance with elevation.
The section’s dictionary reading of 94:7 has the addressee stand upright after finishing; this command tells the Prophet to rise for night worship, a specific parallel in stance and divine address.

The section joins raised remembrance with longing toward the Lord; this verse commands the Prophet to remember his Lord’s name and devote himself wholly to Him, bringing those two features together in a devotional act.
The section moves from raised remembrance to standing and turning toward the Lord; this verse joins remembrance of the Lord’s name to prayer, a compact parallel to that pairing.
The section cites 79:28 for the raised sky; this same creation passage then says the earth was spread out, a specific continuation from upper structure to ground.
Following the section’s 79:28 sky and this passage’s spread earth, this ayah says its water and pasture were brought forth; it adds what the earth provides in that continuing creation scene.

The section develops the raised-sky and erected-mountain landscape in 88:18–20; this nearby creation passage says the mountains were firmly anchored, adding their setting to the sky-and-earth account around 79:28.

The section’s dictionary entry for root ن ق ض concerns undoing what was made solidly; this verse calls the spider’s house the weakest of houses. The contrast between firm construction and a deliberately fragile dwelling is specific, though the verse does not depict it being dismantled.

The section’s root ن ص ب dictionary sense includes setting a stone upright; this verse refers to what is sacrificed upon “النُّصُبِ,” erected cult stones. That is a different religious use of the same set-up-stone branch, marking a boundary from the section’s upright stance.

The section’s root ن ص ب dictionary sense includes setting a stone upright; this verse names “الْأَنْصَابَ,” cult stones, among things forbidden. It shows the same erected-stone branch in a distinct context from the section’s command to stand.
